I have two dogs. The oldest is a four year-old Yellow Lab, and the youngest is a one year-old Golden Retriever.

The Yellow Lab has always had a tendency to itch and scratch herself bald and sometimes cause bloody sores under her armpits, inside of her back legs, directly below her tail, and on the sides of her butt. My parents have always stated that Labs have itchy skin, and it's normal (I highly doubt this).

We recently adopted the Golden Retriever, but we have kept him on his previous diet and dog food that the previous owners fed him. He didn't have any sores when we got him.

Now, both of our dogs will nibble and bite themselves until they bleed and produce sores on their skin. Our Golden Retriever has developed black patches where he would bite, and all of the hair on his abdomen has gone away leaving it bald, with a dark reddish tone and various little red raied bumps all over.

My parents said that he developed his red belly because 'he lays down on the back porch, which is red, and thats why he is hairless and red there now.'

My dogs bite at themselves constantly, and all my parents do is yell at them to stop.

I'm growing really frustrated with my parents lame excuses because I really think there is an environmental factor causing my dogs to react in such a manner.

I am suspecting it's mildew exposure, but I'm having difficulty finding much information online regarding it (This house is pretty nasty, and I have found several parts of the house with mold growing in it, and the parents don't care enough to clean it up).

(Also, my cat wheezes and has a hard time breathing, and shes been around the environment for 14 years. We also have a bad dust problem which leads me to believe the reactions my pets are experincing are based on environmental factors).

My two dogs are biting at their skin until they bleed and develop sores. Help??
Get your house cleaned by professionals or look up how to eliminate fungus growth in the house. It's absolutely an environmental factor.

Take them to the vet! No one in your family or on the internet will be able to ascertain the cause or be able to give them the appropriate exams or tests. I feel so bad for these dogs that they're actually at the point of bleeding now.
Also look at what your dog's are eating. Yeast is your dog's enemy and if there is a lot of byproduct in the food then it can cause for a yeast infection of the skin.
It can be allergies, scabies, skin infections of various sorts or ringworm. Take them to the vet and have a biopsy on the skin done as well as allergy blood tests.
